es.summary: Inflamación de los bronquios, generalmente de origen viral, que produce tos productiva, fiebre leve y disnea. Mejora en días, pero la tos puede persistir semanas.
key_points: Causa más frecuente: virus respiratorios (resfrío, gripe).
Factores irritantes (humo de cigarrillo, contaminación) aumentan el riesgo.
Diagnóstico clínico; radiografía de tórax suele ser normal.
Tratamiento sintomático: hidratación, antitérmicos y broncodilatadores si hay sibilancias.

pathophysiology: Se libera mediadores inflamatorios → edema y aumento de secreción mucosa.
Moco espeso obstruye vías pequeñas, provocando tos y sibilancias.
risk_factors: Humo de cigarrillo, contaminación del aire, polvo y vapores.
Ambientes cerrados y contacto cercano con personas enfermas.
signs_symptoms: Tos productiva con esputo claro o amarillento.
Disnea leve y sibilancias al auscultar.
Dolor o presión torácica y sensación de opresión.
diagnostics: Historia clínica y examen físico con auscultación de crepitantes.
Radiografía de tórax: generalmente sin infiltrados.
Pruebas virales (PCR) si se sospecha infección específica.
treatment: Reposo y aumento de ingesta de líquidos (≥1500 mL/día).
Paracetamol o ibuprofeno para fiebre y dolor.
Humidificador o vapor para aflojar secreciones.
Acetilcisteína nebulizada como mucolítico en secreciones espesas.
complications: Bronquitis crónica o exacerbación de EPOC.
Deshidratación por fiebre y pérdida de secreciones.
nursing_care: Monitorear signos vitales y SpO₂ cada 4 h.
Auscultar pulmones y registrar cambios en ruidos.
Fomentar posición semi‑Fowler para facilitar la expansión pulmonar.
Promover hidratación y uso de humidificador.
Administrar medicamentos según prescripción y observar efectos.
patient_teaching: Beber al menos 1500 mL de líquidos al día y evitar bebidas alcohólicas.
No fumar ni exponerse a humo o contaminantes.
Practicar tos productiva y respiración con labios fruncidos.
Usar inhalador correctamente y registrar dosis.
Buscar atención médica si la fiebre persiste >3 días o hay dificultad respiratoria creciente.

outcomes: Patrón respiratorio eficaz: respiración sin disnea en reposo en 48 h.

interventions.action: Evaluar frecuencia respiratoria y esfuerzo al respirar cada 4 h.
interventions.rationale: Detectar cambios tempranos de deterioro respiratorio.

interventions.action: Auscultar campos pulmonares y registrar ruidos.
interventions.rationale: Identificar presencia de sibilancias o crepitantes.

interventions.action: Colocar al paciente en posición semi‑Fowler.
interventions.rationale: Facilita la expansión pulmonar y reduce el trabajo respiratorio.

interventions.action: Administrar broncodilatador inhalado según indicación.
interventions.rationale: Alivia broncoconstricción y mejora el flujo de aire.

interventions.action: Enseñar técnica de respiración con labios fruncidos.
interventions.rationale: Ayuda a mantener vías abiertas y reduce la disnea.

interventions.action: Fomentar ingesta de líquidos y uso de humidificador.
interventions.rationale: Disuelve secreciones y facilita la expectoración.

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de desequilibrio de volumen de líquidos
outcomes: Balance hídrico mantenido: ingesta ≥ 1500 mL/día en 24 h.
Peso estable: variación ≤ 0,5 kg en 48 h.

interventions.action: Registrar ingesta y eliminación de líquidos cada 8 h.
interventions.rationale: Detectar déficit o exceso de volumen rápidamente.

interventions.action: Ofrecer agua, jugos claros y sopas entre comidas.
interventions.rationale: Aumenta la hidratación y ayuda a fluidificar secreciones.

interventions.action: Evaluar turgencia cutánea y mucosas cada turno.
interventions.rationale: Indicadores clínicos de deshidratación.

interventions.action: Recordar al paciente evitar bebidas con cafeína o alcohol.
interventions.rationale: Reducen la retención de líquidos y aumentan la pérdida urinaria.

interventions.action: Educar sobre la importancia de hidratarse al presentar fiebre o tos.
interventions.rationale: Previene complicaciones por deshidratación.

interventions.action: Notificar al médico si la ingesta es < 1000 mL/día o hay signos de deshidratación.
interventions.rationale: Permite intervención temprana y ajuste de terapia.

en.summary: Inflammation of the bronchi, usually viral in origin, producing productive cough, mild fever, and dyspnea. Improves in days, but cough may persist for weeks.
key_points: Most common cause: respiratory viruses (cold, flu).
Irritating factors (cigarette smoke, pollution) increase risk.
Clinical diagnosis; chest X‑ray usually normal.
Symptomatic treatment: hydration, antipyretics and bronchodilators if wheezing.

pathophysiology: Release of inflammatory mediators → edema and increased mucous secretion.
Thick mucus obstructs small airways, causing cough and wheezing.
risk_factors: Cigarette smoke, air pollution, dust and vapors.
Closed environments and close contact with sick individuals.
signs_symptoms: Productive cough with clear or yellow sputum.
Mild dyspnea and wheezing on auscultation.
Chest pain or pressure and sensation of oppression.
diagnostics: Medical history and physical exam with auscultation of crackles.
Viral tests (PCR) if specific infection suspected.
treatment: Rest and increased fluid intake (≥1500 mL/day).
Paracetamol or ibuprofen for fever and pain.
Humidifier or steam to loosen secretions.
Nebulized acetylcysteine as mucolytic for thick secretions.
complications: Dehydration from fever and loss of secretions.
nursing_care: Monitor vital signs and SpO₂ every 4 h.
Auscultate lungs and record changes in sounds.
Encourage semi‑Fowler position to facilitate lung expansion.
Promote hydration and use of humidifier.
Administer medications as prescribed and observe effects.
patient_teaching: Drink at least 1500 mL of fluids per day and avoid alcoholic beverages.
Do not smoke or expose yourself to smoke or contaminants.
Practice productive cough and pursed‑lip breathing.
Use inhaler correctly and record doses.
Seek medical attention if fever persists >3 days or if breathing difficulty increases.

outcomes: Effective breathing pattern: breathing without dyspnea at rest within 48 h.

interventions.action: Assess respiratory rate and effort every 4 h.
interventions.rationale: Detect early changes in respiratory deterioration.

interventions.action: Auscultate lung fields and record sounds.
interventions.rationale: Identify presence of wheezing or crackles.

interventions.action: Place patient in semi‑Fowler position.
interventions.rationale: Facilitates lung expansion and reduces work of breathing.

interventions.action: Administer inhaled bronchodilator as indicated.
interventions.rationale: Relieves bronchoconstriction and improves airflow.

interventions.action: Teach pursed‑lip breathing technique.
interventions.rationale: Helps keep airways open and reduces dyspnea.

interventions.action: Encourage fluid intake and use of humidifier.
interventions.rationale: Dilutes secretions and facilitates expectoration.

outcomes: Maintained fluid balance: intake ≥ 1500 mL/day in 24 h.
Stable weight: variation ≤ 0.5 kg in 48 h.

interventions.action: Record fluid intake and output every 8 h.
interventions.rationale: Detect deficit or excess volume quickly.

interventions.action: Offer water, clear juices and soups between meals.
interventions.rationale: Increases hydration and helps fluidify secretions.

interventions.action: Assess skin turgor and mucous membranes each shift.
interventions.rationale: Clinical indicators of dehydration.

interventions.action: Remind patient to avoid caffeinated or alcoholic beverages.
interventions.rationale: Reduce fluid retention and increase urine output.

interventions.action: Educate on importance of hydration when fever or cough present.
interventions.rationale: Prevents complications from dehydration.

interventions.action: Notify physician if intake < 1000 mL/day or signs of dehydration appear.
interventions.rationale: Allows early intervention and therapy adjustment.

summary.1.quote: Most cases of acute bronchitis get better within several days.

key_points.0.quote: The same viruses that cause colds and the flu often cause acute bronchitis.

key_points.1.quote: Being exposed to tobacco smoke, air pollution, dust, vapors, and fumes can also cause acute bronchitis.

sections.pathophysiology.2.quote: It causes a cough that often brings up mucus.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: Symptoms can be worsened by respiratory viruses such as influenza.

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: Being exposed to tobacco smoke, air pollution, dust, vapors, and fumes can also cause acute bronchitis.

sections.risk_factors.3.quote: These viruses spread through the air when people cough, or through physical contact (for example, on unwashed hands).

sections.treatment.2.quote: A humidifier or steam can also help.

sections.treatment.4.quote: Acetylcysteine is used to help clients clear thick, tenacious mucus from the airways.

sections.complications.1.quote: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a group of conditions that cause the blockage of air flow and result in breathing issues.

sections.nursing_care.3.quote: Treatments include rest, fluids, and aspirin (for adults) or acetaminophen to treat fever.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: Being exposed to tobacco smoke, air pollution, dust, vapors, and fumes can also cause acute bronchitis.
